risks.reasoning: For the year ended 31 December 2019, the consolidated cash flow statement reports net cash used in operating activities of HK$58,342 thousand and year-end cash and cash equivalents presented in the cash flow statement of HK$9,529 thousand. Using the protocol cash definition and monthly operating cash burn of HK$58,342 thousand / 12, runway is approximately 1.96 months, below the 3-month critical threshold. Note 21 reconciles the HK$9,529 thousand cash-flow-statement balance to statement-of-financial-position cash and bank overdraft, so pledged time deposits are not added back.
risks.calculation_method: Cash runway = cash-flow-statement cash and cash equivalents / (absolute annual net cash used in operating activities / 12).

risks.reasoning: The accountants' report shows comparable annual profits attributable to owners of HK$30,633 thousand, HK$40,169 thousand and HK$33,675 thousand for 2017, 2018 and 2019 respectively. There are zero loss periods, so the continuous-loss condition is not met.
risks.calculation_method: Record and count comparable annual profit/loss periods; no arithmetic risk calculation is required.

risks.reasoning: Audited revenue increased from HK$552,652 thousand in 2017 to HK$768,145 thousand in 2018 and HK$879,401 thousand in 2019. Comparable growth is approximately +38.99% and +14.48%, so neither the negative-growth medium threshold nor the <=-20% high threshold is met.
risks.calculation_method: Comparable annual revenue growth = (current-year revenue - prior-year revenue) / prior-year revenue.

risks.reasoning: For the year ended 31 December 2019, the largest customer generated HK$402,087 thousand and the top five customers generated HK$852,733 thousand against audited total revenue of HK$879,401 thousand. Recalculated concentration is approximately 45.72% for the largest customer and 96.97% for the top five; the top-five share exceeds the 80% high threshold.
risks.calculation_method: Largest-customer concentration = largest-customer revenue / total revenue; top-five concentration = top-five customer revenue / total revenue.

risks.reasoning: The five largest supplier shares sum to 38.0% in 2017, 37.9% in 2018 and 24.9% in 2019; the largest supplier shares are 17.4%, 19.0% and 11.5% respectively. All are below the frozen medium thresholds of 30% for the largest supplier and 60% for the top five.
risks.calculation_method: For each comparable year, take the maximum disclosed individual supplier share and sum the five disclosed individual supplier shares to recompute top-five concentration.

risks.reasoning: The complete corporate history and reorganization disclosure shows Fate Investment was wholly owned by Mr Wu, the issuer became wholly owned by Fate Investment, and the pre-offering group structure remained a 100% ownership chain. No actual pre-IPO investor redemption, repurchase, put, restoration or other special right was identified. Generic corporate-law redemption or share-buyback provisions are not treated as actual investor rights.

A landlord-tenant dispute resulted in an adverse judgment of about HK$0.3 million plus litigation costs; after legal advice the group estimated it might bear about HK$0.9 million, but the exact cost would only be known after the appeal. At the latest practicable date the appeal remained pending and no final judgment had been made. Because resolution and final materiality remained uncertain, the protocol requires needs_review with provisional medium severity. Separately, the company states there were no material or systemic non-compliance matters.

The group is an established Hong Kong contractor with more than 15 years of operating history and generated substantial revenue from fit-out and repair and maintenance services in each of 2017-2019. It had completed 20 fit-out projects and had 39 projects on hand at the latest practicable date; it also states it did not engage in any material R&D activities. The core business is therefore already commercialized and revenue-generating.
